passage:
This educational game feels more
like therapy than fun.

Game score: 5.0 (Mediocre)

Good points
Could be put to good use in children’s hospitals
and preschools!

Bad points
May be less than two hours of playtime.
Totally unimaginative presentation.
If you don’t need homework, you don’t
need this game.

The Brain Train is a bad name for a
brain training game. For one thing, it’s
misleading. Is it to train the brain or
is it about trains? And it’s dull. Think
Tanks! Now, that’s a fun title. But The
Brain Train is no fun at all, and not just
in name.

The aim of this puzzle game is to see if
two pictures are the same or different.
Some challenge! This isn’t a real game.
It’s Spot the Difference, a bit like the ones
your teacher gave you in kindergarten.
There are better ones on the puzzle page
of the Sunday comics.

It offers to improve the ‘right side of the
brain’. You might not be sure if this means
the right-hand side or the correct side of
your brain. I found out! The right side of
the brain controls ‘artistic, strategic and
imaginative functions’. Does this mean
The Brain Train will make the right side
of the brain larger? You will become
more artistic!

But if you’re looking for a good time,
this is more like homework. At least in
kindergarten you could get gold stars.
Eventually, the differences become so
tiny that you either run out of time looking
for them or guess incorrectly too many
times and bingo! You lose. It gets boring
very quickly.
